audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers gave Neeko Levels 1 through 6 outright (Neeko x5 / Skill / Skill), but the page's own whys contradict that in three of those rows: whys[0] 'neither of you kills', whys[1] "it's even", whys[2] 'it stays a wash', whys[4] 'a clean dodge or early Wither makes it even'. The packet chart agrees with the whys, not the sides. Separately full:diff read 'EVEN' while diffRating, tone and breakdown.difficulty all said Favoured 4/10 — against a 40% win rate.
audit.why: Nasus has one of the safest Level 1s in the game and no all-in until Sheen, so the early rows are genuinely even rather than Neeko-owned; Neeko's real edge is the stackless window at 4-5 and her Level 6 before Sheen. Calling a 40% matchup 'Favoured 4/10' with a green tone is the single most misleading thing on the page.
audit.corrected: Skill / Skill / Skill / Neeko / Skill / Nasus / Skill, proposed as matched full+content pairs with ratings. diff EVEN -> TRICKY, tone to orange, diffRating 4/10 -> 6/10, carryRating 5/10 -> 7/10, and the two prose ratings lines updated to match.

audit.why: spikes[] carries all four entries and the timings are the right ones: Neeko's Level 6 pre-Sheen window, his Sheen+Wither first item, her 4-5 stack-denial shove, and his late 200-stack Q. Note the array is not in chronological order (Lvl 6, 1st item, Lvl 4-5, Late) but each entry's 'when' is correct, so the page renders truthfully.

audit.whatIsWrong: (a) whys[2] and early both credit Nasus's sustain to 'R lifesteal'. The life steal is Soul Eater (P); Fury of the Sands (R) grants health, attack range, armour, MR and reduced Q cooldown, not life steal. (b) dosFull[2] says 'Save E to interrupt Wither' — Wither is a point-and-click decaying debuff with no cast to interrupt, so the root does nothing to it. (c) mid implies he can 'Wither you mid-leap' to answer Pop Blossom. (d) tradeBad and dontsFull[1..2] warn about 'a mobile champion' and 'whiffing it into a dash' — Nasus has no dash.
audit.why: The Soul Eater error tells the player his sustain only matters after 6, so they poke into it for five levels. The Wither-interrupt line has the player hold a 12s root against a spell it cannot touch — the mirror audit flagged the same family of claim from Nasus's side and called it the kind of error a player acts on directly.
audit.corrected: Soul Eater (P) is the life steal and it is online from Level 1. Wither (15/14/13/12/11s, 700 range) cannot be interrupted and does not cancel Pop Blossom; the actual counter to your ult is that he walks out of its 600 radius during the preparation, which is why the disguise matters. Nasus is immobile — E whiffs cost you peel, not a chase.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on the page tells the player that Fury of the Sands deals percent-max-health damage, so building health or raw resists against him is the wrong answer.
audit.why: Flagged in missingInteractions as resistances-invalidated, and the R also grants him armour and MR while it rages — so the fight gets worse on both ends of the trade.
audit.corrected: Folded into wants.foe[2]: his ult gives percent-max-health damage plus resists, then the stacked Q finishes through Wither.

edits.before: Level 6 is your one real kill window: land Tangle-Barbs (E) at max distance for the long root, then Q on top and Pop Blossom for the stun-burst before he has Sheen and a stack pile. Set the ult up with Shapesplitter (W) invisibility or a clone so the channel lands unseen — if he sees the wind-up he just steps out or Withers you mid-leap. Through levels 4-5 keep shoving with Q to deny stacks; denying farm here matters more than the kill, because every stack he misses now is damage that won't one-shot you later.

notes: SAMPLE SIZE: the brief's top-level 'games' is 283 but packet.games is 10 and the 40% win rate is drawn from those 10. I used the win rate only as a tiebreak against the page's own whys, which independently describe an even early lane and a Nasus-favoured first item — both point the same way. If the 283 figure is the real one, the direction of the chart is unchanged but 6/10 could be revisited. VOICE: this matchup's content strings are first person ('I', 'my') while the full layer is second person; the mirror auditor flagged the same inconsistency from Nasus's side. I preserved each string's existing voice rather than converting, but the Nasus set needs one deliberate pass. phases[3] and phases[6] and their win[] rows already match the packet chart and were left untouched.
